About

Every screen, sentence, and story has one purpose

I am a UX Writer and Content Strategist with 8+ years of experience crafting meaningful content across digital products, healthcare, fintech, sports, education, entertainment, and brand communication.

My journey started with storytelling. Before entering the world of UX, I explored filmmaking as a writer, director, and actor, which helped me understand human emotions, audience behaviour, and the power of narratives. That foundation continues to influence my work today, where I transform complex ideas into simple, intuitive, and engaging user experiences.

Throughout my career, I have worked across different forms of communication, from writing product experiences and multilingual content to creating training films, brand stories, educational books, advertising campaigns, and creative narratives.

I believe great content is not just about words; it is about understanding people. Whether it is helping a user complete a task, making learning more engaging, or telling a brand’s story, my approach is rooted in empathy, clarity, and storytelling.

Beyond UX, I continue to explore creativity through filmmaking, poetry, storytelling, AI-powered music experiments, and writing about UX and current affairs.

For me, every screen, sentence, and story has one purpose: to create a connection between people and ideas.

Nov 2025 to present

UX Writer & Localisation Specialist · Dimensions NXG Pvt. Ltd.

Project 1: B by Lenskart | Smart AI glasses

iOS: App Store · Android: Google Play

My role

I was the only UX Writer on the B by Lenskart project, owning the content from start to finish. I worked closely with the Product Manager and UI/UX Designer in Figma to create clear, consistent copy across the app, including onboarding, device status messages, error states, empty states, and other key user touchpoints.

The problem

During UAT, I went beyond the pass/fail results and observed how people actually interacted with the product. Two issues stood out:

Issue (i)Users were unsure what some instructions were asking them to do.
Issue (ii)Many users struggled to understand what the glasses’ LED light indicators meant, causing hesitation and mistakes.
Solution

As the only writer on the project, I took ownership of these issues. I simplified the copy, made instructions more direct, and improved the LED status messages so users could understand them quickly and continue with confidence.

Project 2: MAI Smart healthband designed for women

Android: Google Play

My role

I was the sole UX Writer for Mai, responsible for the app’s content from end to end. My work included onboarding, tooltips, health insights, error messages, and Hindi localisation. I worked closely with the Product Manager and UI/UX Designer to ensure every piece of content was simple, clear, and easy to understand.

User research

Rather than making assumptions about rural users, I participated in field research in Khapa Village, Madhya Pradesh, where many Mai users come from. Speaking directly with women helped me understand how they interpreted health information and interacted with the app.

I realised the challenge wasn’t just translating English into Hindi. It was making health information easy to understand for people who weren’t familiar with medical or app-related terminology.

Solution

I first simplified the English copy by removing technical and medical jargon. Then I localised it into natural, conversational Hindi instead of translating it word for word.

The goal was simple: every user should be able to read the content, understand it instantly, and know what to do next without confusion.

Feb 2024 to Nov 2025

UX Writer & Localisation Specialist · Sporta Technologies Pvt. Ltd.

Project 1: Dream11

iOS: App Store · Android: Google Play

My role

At Dream11, I worked as a UX Writer and Localisation Specialist, creating content for the app across English, Hindi, and Marathi. My work included UX copy, push notifications, in-app nudges, feature communication, and localisation. I collaborated closely with Product Managers, Designers, Marketing, and Engineering teams to ensure a consistent user experience across every touchpoint.

The challenge

Fantasy sports can be difficult for first-time users to understand. One of my biggest responsibilities was simplifying complex concepts like How to Play, Fantasy Points System, and contest rules into language that was easy to read and act on.

Another challenge was keeping users engaged throughout live tournaments. Since every match has different timings, teams, and contests, push notifications and in-app nudges had to be updated quickly while remaining relevant and actionable. The goal was to encourage users to create teams before contests filled up without making the communication feel repetitive or intrusive.

A significant portion of Dream11’s audience comes from Tier 2, Tier 3, and Tier 4 cities. This meant localisation was much more than translation. Every message had to feel natural in English, Hindi, and Marathi while preserving the excitement and energy of the original content.

What I worked on
  • UX copy for key user journeys
  • Push notifications and in-app nudges
  • “How to Play” and Fantasy Points educational content
  • Contest and match-related communication
  • English, Hindi, and Marathi localisation
  • Linguistic QA and copy reviews
My approach

I focused on making every piece of content simple, actionable, and easy to understand. Instead of translating word for word, I adapted the copy to suit each language and audience, ensuring users could quickly understand the message and take the intended action without confusion.

Driving engagement through localised campaigns

Beyond match reminders and contest updates, I planned and wrote culturally relevant push notification campaigns to connect with users in their preferred language.

For occasions such as Marathi Bhasha Gaurav Din, Maharashtra Day, and Hindi Bhasha Diwas, I created English, Hindi, and Marathi push notifications to remind users that Dream11 was available in their native language.

The objective wasn’t just to celebrate these occasions. It was to help users who found English language difficult discover that they could enjoy the app in a language they were more comfortable with. This made the product feel more familiar, accessible, and inclusive.

Instead of translating the same message across languages, I adapted the tone and wording to suit each audience while preserving the intent and excitement of the campaign.

These localisation-led campaigns received strong user engagement and reinforced the importance of communicating with users in the language they understand best.

May 2023 to Feb 2024

Script Writer · Wellness Forever Medicare Ltd.

Transforming Training Content into Engaging Learning Experiences

As a Script Writer at Wellness Forever Medicare Ltd., I created training and promotional content for FMCG and Pharma operations, focusing on making complex information easier, more engaging, and memorable for employees.

The primary audience included Customer Service Associates, store employees, store managers, area managers, and warehouse teams. Since training videos were often perceived as routine and boring, I focused on changing the learning experience by blending education with storytelling, humour, and real workplace situations.

My approach

I conceptualised and scripted training videos by combining:

  • Storytelling techniques from filmmaking and screenwriting
  • Humour and relatable workplace scenarios to maintain attention
  • Character-driven narratives to make learning more memorable
  • Creative direction, acting insights, and voiceover supervision to improve script-to-screen execution

I collaborated with video production teams to develop storyboards, dialogues, and training modules that aligned with brand communication goals while keeping employees engaged.

Impact

The initial video completion and viewing percentage was in the single digits. By introducing a more entertaining and story-led approach, the content became more relatable and enjoyable for employees.

The engagement rate increased significantly, reaching 87% viewership in just 3 months, with employees actively returning to watch training videos regularly.

This experience strengthened my belief that even functional content can become powerful when designed around human emotions, storytelling, and user behaviour.

Freelancing work

Brand copy with a point of view

1. Zomato

Ad issue
  • ‘MC’ and ‘BC’ were meant as shortform for Mac n’ Cheese and Butter Chicken.
  • But, in Hindi and Marathi ‘MC’ and ‘BC’ are obscene slang terms, so many people found it vulgar and offensive.

This ad created controversy and Zomato faced criticism for it.

My idea:
Copy: Close your Mac (indicating Macbook) and Stop buttering your Boss (office humor)
It’s time to order Mac n’ Cheese or Butter chicken instead
CTA: Order now on Zomato

I prefer creating humor that informs, inspires, or solves problems rather than using vulgarity for attention. That was my Freelancing work.

2. SUN Marathi (SUN TV Network Ltd.)

Building brand identity for a new Marathi entertainment channel

In 2021, Sun TV Network Limited expanded into the Marathi regional entertainment space with the launch of SUN Marathi.

As a new entrant in the market, the channel faced a unique communication challenge. Marathi audiences were already familiar with established entertainment networks like Zee, Star, and Colors, which had built strong recognition through daily soaps, entertainment programming, and additional offerings like news channels.

SUN Marathi needed to create its own identity and establish an emotional connection with Marathi viewers by communicating its core promise as a family entertainment destination featuring daily soaps, Marathi films, and dubbed movie content.

My role

As a freelance Copywriter, I contributed to building SUN Marathi’s communication by developing brand messaging and promotional content.

My key contributions included
  • Created the channel tagline: “सोहळा नात्यांचा”
  • Developed promotional copy for Marathi dubbed film broadcasts
  • Crafted audience-focused communication aligned with Marathi culture, emotions, and entertainment preferences
  • Adapted messaging to build familiarity and trust for a new television brand
Creative approach

The communication focused on positioning SUN Marathi beyond just a television channel. The idea was to present it as a celebration of relationships, emotions, and family entertainment, creating a stronger emotional connection with Marathi households.
